The vitest 5.0.3 installed here has `vi.when` (I checked its type definitions in `node_modules`). You give it a spy and set a result for each set of arguments:

```ts
const spy = vi.fn()
vi.when(spy).calledWith('darkMode').thenReturn(true)
vi.when(spy).calledWith(expect.any(Number)).thenReturn(0)
vi.when(spy).calledWith('user').thenResolve({ id: 1 })  // async
```

By default, a call with arguments you didn't set up falls through to the spy's original implementation. Pass `{ onUnmatched: 'throw' }` as the second argument to make it throw instead. The classic way works in every Vitest version: branch on the arguments inside `mockImplementation`, e.g. `spy.mockImplementation((key) => key === 'darkMode' ? true : 0)`.
